subject: Agriculture
title: How Rocks Become Soil
description: A quick win: understand How Rocks Become Soil.

hook.text: Every soil on Earth started as rock. The journey from boulder to farmable ground takes millennia.

buildup.text: Physical weathering cracks rocks—freeze-thaw cycles, root pressure, and grinding by glaciers.

discovery.text: Chemical weathering dissolves minerals. Rainwater, slightly acidic from CO2, eats granite over centuries.

twist.text: The type of parent rock determines the soil's mineral content. Limestone gives alkaline soil; granite gives acidic.

climax.text: Biological weathering adds the final ingredient—lichens, roots, and microbes break rock into living soil.

punchline.text: Soil is rock—just very, very patient rock.

quiz.question: What role does chemical weathering play in soil formation?
options: It dissolves minerals from rock using acidic rainwater

details.summary: Soil formation begins when rocks are broken down by physical, chemical, and biological weathering over centuries. This topic covers the five soil-forming factors—parent material, climate, organisms, topography, and time—that determine what type of soil develops in any location.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding how soil forms explains why different regions have different soils and agricultural potential. It also reveals why soil is a non-renewable resource on human timescales—once destroyed, it cannot be quickly replaced.
takeaways: Physical weathering breaks rock through freeze-thaw cycles, wind, and root pressure
Chemical weathering dissolves minerals through reactions with water and acids
The five soil-forming factors are parent material, climate, organisms, topography, and time

faq.question: How do rocks become soil over time?
faq.answer: Physical weathering cracks rock through freezing water expansion and root pressure. Chemical weathering dissolves minerals via acidic rainwater and biological acids. Organisms colonize the weathered rock, adding organic matter. Over centuries, these processes create distinct soil layers.

faq.question: Why are the five soil-forming factors important for agriculture?
faq.answer: Parent material determines mineral composition. Climate controls weathering speed and organic matter accumulation. Organisms add fertility. Topography affects drainage and erosion. Time determines soil maturity. Together they explain why Iowa has deep fertile soil while Arizona has thin rocky soil.
